concept: TimePicker is the set window of a clock radio, a recessed well that holds the hour and minute as ink figures, each a field that steps like a detent, with a pair of round set keys under each field and no orange, because a time is a setting and not the unit's loud control.

default_to_avoid.pattern: Material time picker dialog with a round clock face, a sweeping hand and an OK and Cancel bar
default_to_avoid.why_not: A modal clock face hides the unit behind an overlay and asks for a drag on a dial, while P3 asks for parts with a keyboard map and P1 keeps the round part for the one loud control.

default_to_avoid.pattern: native browser time input with its own spinner arrows and clock popup
default_to_avoid.why_not: The browser draws its own stepper and popup in another light and type, and its layout and AM/PM wording change with the browser, so P5's printed label and P6's fixed positions do not hold.

references.source: Braun AB 312 and ABR 21 clock radios (Dietrich Lubs): hour and minute set keys under a time window with tabular digits
Braun DN 40 alarm clock: AM and PM printed beside the digits, the current one marked
WAI-ARIA 1.2 spinbutton role and the APG date picker spin button pattern: one field per unit of time
apps/lab/time-picker/index.html: four renders (LCD window, set well, rotary pair, printed format) in light and dark

derivation.consequence: the display is a live region (polite) and never a control
derivation.form: The time is set in Input's recessed well, not in an LCD window, so the unit's display keeps saying the state and is never focused.

derivation.consequence: tabular numerals, a 7-segment face for LCD values, the system grotesk for OLED text
derivation.form: kind segment draws the figures as 7-segment cells in ink on the well; kind text sets them in the grotesk with tabular figures.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map (arrows step a detent, Home and End reach the ends, Space and Enter press) and a visible value and label
derivation.form: Each field is a spinbutton: arrows step one, PageUp and PageDown step three hours or ten minutes, Home and End reach the ends, and digits type in.

derivation.consequence: keys are round or capsule; rotaries are circles with one index mark; faders ride a groove with a ruler scale
derivation.form: The set keys are IconButton's 44px round keys with a printed minus and plus, one pair standing under the field it moves.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only; links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: The well, figures, keys, focus and the AM or PM mark are ink and plastic, so the unit's one orange control stays the only one.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: Every field has a fixed two-cell width, the period always reserves both words, and typing anything never changes the well's width.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The label is printed above the well on the inset line, and the hint or error is printed below the keys.

options.name: LCD clock window with segment digits and set keys below
set well: Input's recessed well, ink segment figures, a key pair under each field, AM and PM printed with a lamp
pair of rotaries for hour and minute with a printed reading above
Input's well with two numeric fields in grotesk figures and a printed format

variants.reason: B keeps the clock radio's set keys and figures while staying an input-class well, so the display stays the one window that is never a control (P2); A puts a second LCD in the unit and asks people to edit the state window, C spends two round parts that P1 keeps for the loud control and has sixty detents too fine to read, and D is kept as kind text for dense forms.

root.why: The root stacks the printed label, the set well with its keys and the message at fixed positions in one column.

label.why: The label is printed in the label size and medium weight above the well and names the group of fields.

set.why: The set lays the fields and their key pairs on one grid, so each key pair stands under the field it moves.

well.why: The well is a recess with the inverse light and a hairline ring that holds the fields, the same well an Input sits in.

cell.why: Each cell is at least 44px each way, so the field is a full touch target even where the figures draw smaller.

hour.why: The hour sits in the first column at a fixed place, so its key pair can stand right under it.

minute.why: The minute sits in the third column after the colon, at a fixed place over its own key pair.

period.why: The period column reserves both AM and PM at once, so switching the half of the day never shifts the well.

field.why: The field is the spinbutton that takes focus, arrows and typed digits; on kind segment its own text is clear over the figures.

seg.why: The figures are 7-segment cells on Display's pitch, so the set time reads like the clock radio's window.

on.why: Lit segments are the primary ink at full step on the well, at more than 4.5:1 in both themes.

off.why: Unlit segments sit at a quiet step of ink so they show the cell without reading as a lit figure.

colon.why: The colon holds the second column between hour and minute at a fixed width, never moving as values change.

dot.why: On kind segment the colon is two square dots the width of a segment stroke, as on a clock radio.

words.why: AM and PM are printed one above the other inside the period column, like the printing beside a clock's digits.

word.why: Each half of the day is printed in the smallest size in regular weight, in secondary ink at more than 4.5:1.

lit.why: The current half of the day turns primary ink in medium weight with its lamp dot lit, never orange.

keysHour.why: The hour key pair stands under the hour field, two 44px keys with the smallest gap between them.

keysMinute.why: The minute key pair stands under the minute field, two 44px keys with the smallest gap between them.

hint.why: The hint is printed in caption size and secondary ink under the keys and is read with the fields.

error.why: An error is printed in the critical mark colour with a glyph and words, so it never rests on colour alone.

glyph.why: The error glyph is printed flat on the material with the printing stroke at icon size, no shadow.

segment.why: kind segment draws the figures in segments and keeps the field's own text clear over them.

text.why: kind text sets hour and minute in the grotesk at title size with tabular figures, for dense forms.

keys.why: The key row shares the well's columns, padding and hairline width, so every key pair lines up under its field.

focus-within.why: The focused field draws the dark focus ring around its own cell, so it is clear which field the arrows will step.

data-invalid=true.why: An invalid time draws the well's edge in the critical mark colour with words below, never in orange.

data-disabled=true.why: A disabled picker loses the well's inner shadow and fades, while its keys lose their height as disabled keys do.

data-readonly=true.why: A read only picker keeps its figures and focus but hides the set keys, so nothing on it can be stepped.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduce motion each segment turns on or off at once with no fade between figures.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the well gets a real edge, lit segments use the text colour and unlit ones vanish, so the time stays readable.

fill.why: Only a segment's on and off fades, in the segment time, when the field steps to a new value.
